newsitem.title: UK: BOE to use gilt repo in daily ops from March 3.
newsitem.headline: BOE to use gilt repo in daily ops from March 3.

text.p: The Bank of England said on Tuesday it would start using gilt repo in its daily money market operations as part of a package of measures which will come into operation on March 3.
It will continue to use Treasury bills and eligible local authority and bank bills.

The Bank will also broaden the range of counterparties able to participate in its daily operations to include banks, building societies and securities firms, which are active in the gilt repo and/or bill markets.

"These counterparties will not be required to be separately capitalised entities and they will not be subject to special supervision," it said in a statement. The Bank will not publish a list of its money market counterparties, which at present consist of six specialist discount houses.
The Bank will also make changes to its end-of-day arrangements.

"Late repo facilities will be available, typically on an overnight basis, to the settlement banks and, for a transitional period, to the discount houses, to adjust for any end-of-day imbalance in the market," it said.
The changes, first announced in December, are outlined in a paper entitled "Reform of the Bank of England's operations in the sterling money markets."
Several minor technical changes have been made to the original proposals following consultation with market participants.
Final open market operations will be conducted at 2.30 pm, 10 minutes earlier than originally proposed, in order to extend the time available to settle the transactions.

The late repo facility, which the Bank originally proposed to offer at around 3.30 pm, will be made available between 3.50 and 3.55 pm, by which time settlement banks will have a clearer view of their final end-of-day liquidity positions.
Transitional arrangements will be made available for discount houses for up to two years.

"They involve continuing to make available a number of the provisions which are at present applied to the discount houses (including late access to liquidity from the Bank) and which reflect the role they have hitherto played in the Bank's money market operations and the obligations they have undertaken," the Bank said.
The transitional arrangements will be available only to discount houses which remain separately capitalised and subject to special supervisory arrangements.

To avoid any clash between the Bank's 9.45 am money market operations and gilt auctions, the deadline for bids in gilt auctions will be moved from 10.00 am to 10.30 am, starting with auction due on March 26.

The Bank said the changes related to the mechanics of its daily operations and did not alter its basic approach to implementing monetary policy by managing short-term interest rates through open market operations.
